{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg11PCP4gTX7epQDCCTd1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA version of `cholesky` is in place and builds cleanly. It is correct at every size and rank count I tested. It does not scale past two GPUs on this box, though, so the parallel-scalability goal is only partly met.\n\n**What changed** (only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`; nothing created in the project)\n\n- **Distribution:** 256-row blocks dealt cyclically across MPI ranks. Each rank binds to one GPU via its node-local rank and keeps its rows resident on the device.\n- **Algorithm:** blocked left-looking Cholesky. The owner of each diagonal block factors it on the host (OpenMP over rows), then broadcasts the finished L panel. Each rank updates its trailing rows on its GPU with a tiled GEMM and a per-row finishing kernel.\n- **Overlap:** two CUDA streams. The next diagonal block's rows are updated first, so the owner's diagonal work overlaps the bulk of the trailing update. Panels are double-buffered, with events guarding reuse.\n- **OpenMP:** used for host-side work (diagonal factor, panel packing, validation). Each rank's team gets a share of the node's cores; without that split, 4 ranks each spawning 256 threads made the run ~100× slower.\n- **Validation** is distributed: each rank checks its own rows, and the max errors are reduced across ranks. Output format, flags, and exit codes are unchanged, and only rank 0 prints.\n- **CMake:** requires CMake 3.24+ and `native` CUDA architectures by default. MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA are all required unconditionally. The target name is still `cholesky`.\n\n**Numerics**\n\n- The generated matrix is bit-identical to the original (`A` hash matches).\n- Every element is summed over k in the original order. The factor is not bit-identical to the reference, though. The reference's compiler contracts the products into FMA only in some places, and I could not reproduce that pattern with a clean rule. My version uses FMA consistently on host and device. The results agree to rounding: n=1000 summary stats match to all 17 printed digits, and the `-r` hash differs in the last bits.\n- The output is bit-identical across 1–4 ranks and across block widths.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- `-v` passes for n = 1, 7, 100, 130, 300, 513, 1000, 2048, and 2049 at 1–4 ranks.\n- The non-positive-definite path (checked with a debug copy whose diagonal is negated) prints the original message and exits nonzero at 1 and 3 ranks.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090, FP64 peak ≈ 0.56 TFLOPS each; reference at n=2048 is 2130 ms)\n\n| n | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 2048 | 83 ms | — | 112 ms |\n| 8192 | 660 ms | 630 ms | 693 ms |\n| 16384 | 3361 ms | 2446 ms | 2387 ms |\n\nA single GPU reaches roughly 75–80% of the card's FP64 peak at n=16384, so per-GPU kernels are not the problem. The limit is the per-step serial chain: the panel broadcast and the owner's diagonal work run in lockstep. Each rank must receive the full panel every step, which is about n²/2 doubles per rank, and the installed Open MPI is not CUDA-aware, so every panel is staged through host memory.\n\n**Gaps and next steps**\n\n- Scaling past 2 GPUs needs a CUDA-aware MPI, or a lookahead that overlaps the panel broadcast with compute, or a 2D distribution that cuts per-rank communication. I did not implement these.\n- I only had one node, so multi-node runs are untested.\n- Running it requires `mpirun` and at least one CUDA device."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1322,"cache_read_input_tokens":199534,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1322},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0fda21a9-1130-47bb-bc48-7d1a91e00290","uuid":"74572b3f-6e1d-41de-8a40-446e50f858d3","timestamp":"2026-10-13T22:15:05.714Z","request_id":"req_011Cg11PC3EAADs8YDcdTL2G"}
